releases.summary: Restricted-header blocks (CRS 920450) now name the right header, and exceptions for them apply reliably.
notes: Events of CRS 920450/920451 (restricted HTTP headers, such as the If header sent by WebDAV clients) showed an arbitrary header of the request as the location, and exceptions created from them got that header as target, so they applied only some of the time. Each restricted header is now reported on its own, for example REQUEST_HEADERS_NAMES:If.
Exceptions for 920450/920451 with a header target created before 1.0.2 no longer apply: delete them and create them again from a new event, or with the target REQUEST_HEADERS_NAMES:<header>.
A request with two restricted headers now scores both, as the Core Rule Set does.
Header names in exception targets are compared without regard to case.
Installation guide: registry access with your own GitHub account and a classic read:packages token; backup and restore of the project of the folder; a second installation on the same host.

releases.summary: Security updates of the Ubuntu packages in the image.
First release distributed as an image: one image for every component, installed and updated from the registry.
notes: One image, ghcr.io/fzield/waf, runs the control plane, the data plane, the console, the learning engine and the Kubernetes ingress controller, each as its own unprivileged user and group.

Hardened image on Ubuntu 24.04: no shell, no package manager; a component can neither execute nor read the other programs of the image; the control plane, the data plane and the ingress controller cannot start any program at all; read-only file systems and no capabilities in compose.yaml.
The installation kit (compose.yaml, examples, guide, licence) is inside the image: docker run --rm ghcr.io/fzield/waf:1 kit | tar -x -C /opt.
Updates in the console: a daily check for new versions, with their notes and the commands to run (it can be turned off, also with WAF_UPDATE_CHECK=off).
Weekly rebuild with the security updates of Ubuntu, published as a patch release when packages change.
Installations built from the sources move to the image keeping their data (same project name, services, volumes and settings): INSTALLATION.md, "Moving an installation built from the sources".
